To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the power requirement for compression and liquefaction of CO2 streams with impurities is higher than for pure CO2, but can be reduced by increasing the number of compression stages.
the impurities in the CO2 stream have a significant impact on the compression power requirements and the interstage cooling duty.
the power demand for CO2 compression is significantly affected by the presence of impurities in CO2 streams.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a comprehensive model for predicting the power requirements of multistage compression of CO2 streams with varying impurity content and the subsequent liquefaction of CO2 at subcritical pressure.
the development of a thermodynamic model that will provide a detailed insight into the impact of various impurities and the compression strategy on the power demand of a CO2 compression system.
the development of an efficient compression strategy for CO2 streams with impurities and the reduction of the power demand associated with the compression of CO2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of impurities on the compression power demand is not as significant as that on the inter-stage cooling requirements and the liquefaction duty.
the impurity content of CO2 streams originating from various capture options has a significant impact on the compression and transportation costs.

impurities in the CO2 stream can have a significant impact on the power demand of the compression and liquefaction system, and hence the cost of CCS, and that the impact of impurities is strongly dependent on the purity of the feed gas, the pressure at which compression and liquefaction are carried out and the type of compressor technology used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for CO2 streams with high purity, multistage centrifugal compression is the most efficient compression strategy, but for CO2 streams carrying high levels of impurities multistage compression with liquefaction and pumping is a more efficient compression strategy.
impurities in CO2 stream significantly increase the cooling duty for liquefaction and hence the overall power demand.
the impurity content in CO2 streams is a major determinant of the compression power requirements and the associated costs for the transportation of CO2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impurities in CO2 streams originating from various capture routes significantly increase the compression and liquefaction costs.

the impurities in the CO2 streams can have significant effect on the overall compression and liquefaction costs, which can vary by a factor of 1.5 for the range of impurity concentrations considered in our study.
for the compression of CO2 streams containing impurities, liquefaction and subsequent low pressure pumping may offer significant advantages in terms of energy efficiency.
